as_told.title: Mass-spectrometry analysis of the Ubatuba pieces

plain: Some metal fragments known as the Ubatuba fragments, which are said to come from a UFO, were tested at Stanford University, and one of them came back strange: "The magnesium ratios were way off." Magnesium comes in a few natural forms of slightly different weight, and the claim is that the mix of those forms in this piece did not match what is normally found, which would hint that the metal was not made in the ordinary way. The Stanford scientist Garry Nolan tells this himself as one of the people who ran the test. He describes the machine as a highly sensitive mass spectrometer, an instrument that sorts atoms by weight.
